about: The `annual_report_catalogue` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2012 only.

provenance.warning: These figures cite a document not present in the document table, so no address can be given for them. Treat any figure resting on them as uncheckable.

rows.name: Table of contents / department index with page numbers
rows.printed_heading: DEPARTMENT
rows.what_it_is: Alphabetical index of report sections with the printed page number for each, printed beneath the In Memoriam page.
rows.notes: Printed page numbers run 3 lower than the PDF page index.

rows.name: Town at a glance: roads, population, valuation, tax rate and legislative delegation
rows.printed_heading: STATE ROADS: / POPULATION: / DENSITY: / ASSESSED VALUATION: / TAX RATE: / UNITED STATES SENATORS IN CONGRESS: / REPRESENTATIVE IN CONGRESS: / STATE SENATOR: / REPRESENTATIVE IN GENERAL COURT:
rows.what_it_is: Label/value fact block. Carries the 2010 Census population (10,280 — note this differs from the 10,085 printed in the FY2011 report for the same census), the 2012 town census (9982), assessed valuation split, and the FY2013 tax rate.
rows.grain: one town statistic or one officeholder
rows.layout: two-column label/value list; the TOTAL ROADS line is cut off at the top of the page
rows.notes: TAX RATE reads '$ 17.30 (Fiscal 2013)' — the forward year again. Two state representatives are now listed (37th Middlesex and 3rd Worcester), where FY2011 listed one. The 2010 US Census population differs between the two reports for the same census, which is worth flagging to anyone building a population series.

rows.name: Town department office hours
rows.printed_heading: OFFICE HOURS
rows.what_it_is: Opening hours for each town office by day group.
rows.notes: The all-caps footer records the four-day week: '(TOWN HALL, RITTER MEMORIAL BUILDING AND LUNENBURG PUBLIC LIBRARY AND EAGLE HOUSE CLOSED FRIDAY)'. This is the operational consequence of the FY2013 budget described on p20 and can be dated by comparing with the FY2011 hours table.

rows.name: Board and committee regular meeting schedule
rows.what_it_is: When and where each board meets. Continues from page 4.
rows.grain: one board and one recurring meeting slot
rows.notes: Adds a Cemetery Commission row not present in FY2011.

rows.name: Elected officials with term-expiry year
rows.printed_heading: SELECTMEN / BOARD OF HEALTH / BOARD OF ASSESSORS / SEWER COMMISSION / TOWN CLERK / CONSTABLE / SCHOOL COMMITTEE / TRUST FUND COMMISSIONERS / CEMETERY COMMISSIONERS / LIBRARY TRUSTEES / PLANNING BOARD / HOUSING AUTHORITY
rows.what_it_is: Every elected board, its members and each member's term expiry year.
rows.layout: two side-by-side column stacks grouped under board headings
rows.notes: '** denotes chairperson'. Mid-term changes are recorded in the cell text: '2014 David W. Reif resigned (Todd Blake Appt.)' on School Committee, '2013 Vacancy (Richard Storrs)' on Trust Fund Commissioners. Housing Authority separates 'Appointed By Governor:' as its own subheading.

rows.name: Appointed officials, boards and one-year appointments
rows.printed_heading: ASSISTANT BUILDING INSPECTOR / COUNCIL ON AGING-3 YRS / CONSERVATION COMMISSION-3 YRS / HISTORICAL COMMISSION / LOCAL CENSUS LIASON (and the rest of the appointed-office headings)
rows.what_it_is: Every appointed position and committee with appointee and expiry year, including reserve police officers and public weighers.
rows.layout: two to three side-by-side column stacks under committee headings
rows.notes: p8 is 64 lines — the densest page of the front matter.

rows.name: Tax rate recapitulation TOTALS row (orphaned)
rows.what_it_is: A single TOTALS row — percent of total valuation, valuation, tax rate, levy — belonging to a classification / tax-rate recap table whose body is not in the OCR.
rows.layout: one line at the top of p10
rows.notes: The 100.0000 is the point: Lunenburg taxes at a single rate, so all classes carry the full percentage. The body rows that would show the class split are missing. Everything in this row is recoverable from the FY2012 line of the valuation history table below it.

rows.name: Valuation and Tax History, FY2005-FY2012
rows.printed_heading: Valuation and Tax History / Fiscal Year | Tax Rate | Total Valuation | Accounts | Tax Levy | Change(%)
rows.what_it_is: Eight years of tax rate, valuation, account count, levy and year-on-year levy change.
rows.columns: Fiscal Year | Tax Rate | Total Valuation | Accounts | Tax Levy | Change(%)
rows.notes: FY2012: rate 16.83, valuation 1,120,966,561, 5,351 accounts, levy 18,865,867.23, +4.7707%. Every overlapping year matches the FY2011 report exactly, so the two years' tables can be chained without reconciliation.

rows.name: Abstract of assessments by property class
rows.printed_heading: Fiscal Year 2011 Abstract of Assessments / Property Class Code/Description | Accts | Class Valuation | Avg. Value
rows.what_it_is: Assessed valuation by DOR property class code, with account counts and average value.
rows.columns: Property Class Code/Description | Accts | Class Valuation | Avg. Value
rows.notes: THE PRINTED HEADING IS WRONG IN THE SOURCE: it says 'Fiscal Year 2011' but the TOTALS row is 1,120,966,561, which is the FY2012 total from the valuation history immediately above (FY2011 was 1,114,282,889). The figures are FY2012's. Do not join on the heading. As in FY2011, most account counts are missing from the OCR — only Mixed Use (40), Three Family (7) and Apartments (7) print a count — while every valuation and average value is present, so counts can be recovered by division.

rows.name: Assessor's account for exemptions, abatements and overlay, five years
rows.printed_heading: Assessor's Account for Exemptions and Abatements / Description | FY2012 | FY2011 | FY2010 | FY2009 | FY2008
rows.what_it_is: Overlay raised, deficits, charges, potential liability and amount released, FY2008-FY2012.
rows.grain: one overlay line item across five years
rows.columns: Description | FY2012 | FY2011 | FY2010 | FY2009 | FY2008
rows.notes: The FY2011 and FY2010 columns here DISAGREE with the same columns in the FY2011 report: 'Charges to 6/30/2010' FY2010 reads 116,250.15 here and 112,378.97 there; 'Amount Released' FY2011 reads 4,385.99 here and 119,992.49 there. Prior-year columns are evidently restated. Use the year's own report for its own year.

rows.name: New growth revenue by fiscal year, FY2004-FY2011
rows.printed_heading: New Growth Revenue / Fiscal Year | Added Valuation | Tax Rate | New Revenues | Change%)
rows.what_it_is: Valuation added by new construction, the rate applied, revenue produced and change on the prior year.
rows.columns: Fiscal Year | Added Valuation | Tax Rate | New Revenues | Change%)
rows.notes: The table STOPS AT FY2011 — the FY2012 report reprints the FY2011 report's table unchanged rather than adding a FY2012 row. There is no published new-growth figure for FY2012 anywhere in this document, though the finance committee narrative on p20 says new growth is expected to add $350K.

rows.name: Persons buried this year, by month
rows.printed_heading: The following is a list of persons who were buried this year. / NAME | AGE | CEMETERY / JANUARY / FEBRUARY / MARCH / APRIL / MAY / JUNE / JULY / AUGUST / SEPTEMBER / OCTOBER / NOVEMBER / DECEMBER
rows.what_it_is: Every burial in the town cemeteries during 2012 with age and cemetery, grouped by month. War service appended to some names.
rows.layout: printed 180 degrees out — the column header row is the LAST line of the page, months run bottom-to-top, and the two side-by-side month stacks are mirrored
rows.notes: Rotation still wrong. Names, ages and N/S cemetery codes are all legible but they are on different lines from one another — an age on line N belongs to a name on line N or N+1 and there is no reliable rule. '*Denotes Cremation' at what is visually the top. The column header explicitly names the third column CEMETERY, which resolves the unexplained N/S column in the FY2011 version of this table.

rows.name: Capital plan items approved at the 2012 Annual Town Meeting
rows.printed_heading: CAPITAL PLANNING TOWN REPORT / The following items were presented in the Plan. / DEPARTMENT   ITEM   AMOUNT
rows.what_it_is: The eleven capital items in the FY13 plan, by department, with amounts. Introduced by 'At the Annual Town Meeting May 2012, $464,487.00 was approved for Capital Requests.'
rows.printed_total: $464,487.00 was approved for Capital Requests (stated in the narrative above the table)
rows.notes: THE COLUMNS ARE OUT OF ORDER RELATIVE TO THEIR OWN HEADER: the header reads DEPARTMENT / ITEM / AMOUNT but the rows read department, amount, item. A stray '9' (the printed page number) has landed inside the last row. Largest items: School Dept. Passios roof re-seaming $107,920; Technology Dept. $75,517; School Dept. mobile media carts $64,500. Article 16 on p84 gives the funding detail — $439,193 raised and appropriated plus eleven named prior-article transfers totalling $464,487, which is a genuine self-check on this table.

rows.name: Nashoba Environmental Health Department activity counts
rows.printed_heading: Environmental Health Department / Environmental Information Responses / Lunenburg Office (days)... / Food Service Licenses & Inspections... / Beach/Camp Inspections... / Housing & Nuisance Investigations... / Septic System Test Applications... / Septic System Lot Tests. / Septic System Plan Applications.. / Septic System Consultations....... / Well Permits. / Water Quality/Well Consultations......
rows.what_it_is: Counts of regional health district activity for Lunenburg, each with an explanatory paragraph.
rows.layout: label with dot leaders, count right
rows.notes: Much better recovered than FY2011's version. Lunenburg Office (days) 18, Food Service 31, Beach/Camp 39, Housing & Nuisance 28, Septic Plan Applications 33, Septic Construction Inspections 4, Well Permits 7. Two counts are still lost in the leaders (Septic System Test Applications, Water Quality/Well Consultations) and one — 'Septic System Lot Tests. 0131333799.77' — is OCR garbage and must not be used. The narrative on p15 separately reports 51 Title 5 private septic inspections reviewed.

rows.name: Nashoba Nursing Service & Hospice visit and clinic counts
rows.printed_heading: Nashoba Nursing Service & Hospice / Home Health / Nursing Visits / Home Health Aide Visits / Rehabilitative Therapy Visit / Medical Social Service Visits / Hospice Volunteer and Spiritual Care Visits....... / CLINICS / Local Well Adult, Support Groups, & Other Clinic Visits..
rows.what_it_is: Home health visits by discipline and clinic attendance for Lunenburg residents.
rows.layout: label with dot leaders, count right
rows.notes: EVERY COUNT IS PRESENT this year, unlike FY2011: Nursing Visits 1177, Home Health Aide 405, Rehabilitative Therapy 551, Medical Social Service 35, Hospice Volunteer/Spiritual 23, Clinic Visits 404, Flu Clinic attendance 191, Well Adult Clinic 176. The 'Number of patients whom received Vaccine ....2' line is as implausible as its FY2011 counterpart and is probably a truncated three-digit number.

rows.name: Communicable disease cases reported
rows.printed_heading: Communicable Disease / Communicable Disease Number of Cases / Confirmed
rows.what_it_is: Reportable disease cases among Lunenburg residents.
rows.notes: NEW — in FY2011 every one of these counts was lost. Campylobacter 1, Giardia 2, Group B streptococcus 1, Hepatitis C 4, Influenza 10, Lyme Disease 5, Salmonella 1, Yersiniosis 1. These sum to 25, which ties to the printed 'Confirmed 25'. THE PAGE PRINTS THE SAME TABLE TWICE (lines 2-10 and lines 24-32) with identical disease counts but a DIFFERENT 'Health Promotion / Skilled Nursing' figure — 28 in the first copy and 14 in the second. One of the two is wrong and nothing on the page says which.

rows.name: Nashoba Dental Health Department: school dental programme counts
rows.printed_heading: Dental Health Department / Examination, Cleaning & Fluoride - Grades K, 2 & 4 / Students Eligible.... / Students Participating / Referred to Dentist.... / Instruction - Grades K, 1 & 5 / Number of Programs...
rows.what_it_is: Children eligible for, participating in and referred out of the school dental hygiene programme.
rows.layout: label with dot leaders, count right
rows.notes: Students Eligible 352, Students Participating 228, Referred to Dentist 26, Number of Programs 10. Complete, unlike FY2011 where the eligible count had drifted into a sentence.

rows.name: Library statistics for 2012
rows.printed_heading: Oh right, I promised those numbers to you - here they are for 2012:
rows.what_it_is: The library's headline operating statistics as a bulleted list.
rows.layout: bulleted list, two bullets per line in places
rows.notes: NEW — the equivalent block in FY2011 is missing from the OCR entirely. 5th highest per capita appropriation among 12 similar-sized towns at $33.63 per capita; 70% of residents registered; open 2,178 hours; close to 200 programmes; over 2,000 volunteer hours; 70,218 volumes of which 46,789 books; over 21,982 interlibrary loans; circulation 116,429 items, 78,230 books and 25,131 videos. NOTE the circulation figure is printed with a dollar sign — '$116,429 items' — which is a typo in the source, not a currency amount. Several bullets are doubled up on one line and must be split.

rows.name: Roster of the Lunenburg Fire Department
rows.printed_heading: Roster of the Lunenburg Fire Department
rows.what_it_is: Every member of the fire department with rank and EMS certification, plus a high school intern.
rows.layout: centred officer block then two side-by-side alphabetical columns
rows.notes: '*Indicates member of Specialized Rescue Teams including Dive, Cave In and Confined Space Rescue Teams'. Abbreviations change from FY2011: 'Firefighter/EMT' becomes 'FF/EMT'. New chief (Patrick A. Sullivan) after Scott Glenny's retirement.

rows.name: Police Department FY13 staff roster
rows.printed_heading: PY13 Stair [FY13 Staff]
rows.what_it_is: Police department personnel by rank — chief, lieutenant, patrol supervisors, detectives, patrol officers, reserve intermittent officers.
rows.layout: centred rank headings with names beneath; patrol and reserve officers run as comma-separated prose
rows.notes: The heading is OCR rubble ('PY13 Stair'). Vacancies are recorded as rows ('Detective Sergeant (Vacancy)'). Two ranks are 'Acting Sergeant'. Also on this page: a nine-item departmental Goals list.

rows.name: Police calls for service, 2009-2012, and incidents by category
rows.printed_heading: Calls For Service / Crimes against the person | Crimes against property | General Assistance | Motor Vehicle Stops / • 2009 • 2010 • 2011 • 2012
rows.what_it_is: Two charts side by side: a four-year line/bar of total calls for service, and a grouped bar chart of four incident categories by year.
rows.grain: one year (left chart); one category and year (right chart)
rows.layout: two charts with axis labels and scattered data labels
rows.notes: Four data labels survive on the left chart — 12670, 10175, 10044, 9558 — but which year each belongs to is NOT recoverable from the OCR, and the narrative saying calls were '8% higher than the previous year' does not fit a falling series, so the labels may be mis-ordered on the page. The right chart has axis labels and a legend but NO data values. The narrative beneath carries the usable numbers: general assistance up 14%, disturbances up 6%, firearms licensing up 67%, crimes against people down 10%, crimes against property down 3%.

rows.name: Sewer system connection counts
rows.what_it_is: Counts of properties connected, connectable and newly connected to the town sewer.
rows.notes: 673 properties connected, 387 with access but not connected, 35 new connections during 2012. A rare published denominator for the sewer enterprise fund.

rows.name: School Committee membership, meeting schedule and Central Office personnel
rows.printed_heading: Superintendent of Schools / Central Office Personnel / Regular Meetings / School Personnel/Business Services / Technology/Network Services / Transportation Services / Cafeteria Services / Special Education Services / Facilities & Grounds / Extended Day/School Linked Services
rows.what_it_is: School Committee members and the district's central office staff grouped by function.
rows.grain: one committee member or central office employee
rows.layout: two-column staff block grouped by office
rows.notes: The Technology Director is recorded as 'shared with the Town' — the same person appears in the town's technology line, which matters when reading either budget. Third-Wednesday meetings have moved from Brooks House to Thomas C. Passios.

rows.name: District enrollment by grade level, October 2010 - October 2012
rows.printed_heading: Enrollment: October 1, 2010 - October 1, 2012 / Grade Level | 10/01/10 | 10/01/11 | 10/01/12
rows.what_it_is: Head count by grade for three successive Octobers.
rows.notes: Three grade labels are missing (the rows for grades 6 and 8, and one other) and must be inferred from position; PK and Ungraded have no 10/01/12 value. The columns sum to the printed totals, which is a check. The narrative gives the composition of the 1613: 1532 Lunenburg residents, 52 school choice, 29 under the non-resident agreement with Shirley; 286 students with disabilities (17.7%); 24 placed outside the district, 19 day and 5 residential, of the day placements 7 in a Collaborative. That out-of-district placement COUNT is exactly the number the standing questions say is unpublished — it is published here.

rows.name: Lunenburg Primary School staff roster with room numbers
rows.what_it_is: Primary school staff by grade and role, each with a room number.
rows.layout: two side-by-side column stacks, room number in the left-hand gutter of each
rows.notes: Room numbers are a separate column here (they were part of the name string in the FY2011 THMS roster). Several rows have the room number and the name on different lines. Section headings (Pre-School, Second Grade, Third Grade, Achieve, Physical Education/Health) are legible.

rows.name: Turkey Hill Middle School MCAS: percent advanced or proficient, school against state
rows.printed_heading: % of STUDENTS SCORING IN THE ADVANCED/PROFICIENT RANGE / GRADE | SUBJECT | THMS | STATE
rows.what_it_is: Spring 2012 MCAS results for the middle school against the state, by grade and subject. This is the first year THMS covers grades 4-7 after the district consolidation.
rows.notes: Grade 4 ELA 58/57, Grade 4 Math 60/51, Grade 5 ELA 71/61, Grade 5 Math 77/57, Grade 5 Sci/Tech 70/52, Grade 6 ELA 80/66, Grade 6 Math 69/60, Grade 7 ELA 75/67, Grade 7 Math 63/51. One grade cell (row 6, ELA) is blank and must be inferred. THE GRADE RANGE CHANGED between FY2011 (grades 6-8) and FY2012 (grades 4-7) because the district consolidated from four schools to three, so a THMS series across the two years is not comparing the same population.

rows.name: Turkey Hill Middle School staff roster
rows.printed_heading: THMS STAFF ROSTER
rows.what_it_is: Middle school staff by role, including tutors, aides, custodial and cafeteria.
rows.notes: Support roles are typed precisely ('1:1 Tutor', 'Wilson Tutor', '1:1 Aide'), which is more detail than any other year's roster gives.

rows.name: Lunenburg High School 2012 MCAS results with state rank
rows.printed_heading: Lunenburg High School - 2012 MCAS Results / Subject Test | Advanced/Proficient | State Rank | Percentile in State
rows.what_it_is: Grade 10 MCAS results by subject, with the school's rank among Massachusetts high schools and its state percentile band.
rows.columns: Subject Test | Advanced/Proficient | State Rank | Percentile in State
rows.notes: ELA 100% / 1 of 348 / Top 1%; Math 91% / 73 of 348 / Top 21%; Science 82% / 114 of 341 / Top 33%. The State Rank column — a rank out of a stated denominator — appears in no other year catalogued here and is the most quotable line in the school section. 41 seniors received Adams Scholarships.

rows.name: Lunenburg High School faculty and staff roster 2012-2013
rows.printed_heading: Faculty/Staff Roster / 2012-2013
rows.what_it_is: High school staff by department with department liaisons flagged.
rows.layout: two side-by-side column stacks under department headings
rows.notes: Roles beyond teaching are recorded in the second column ('Greenhouse Asst.', 'AD', 'Athletic Secretary', 'Dept. Liaison'). Timothy Macuga is listed under both Language Arts and Social Studies.

rows.name: School facilities: capital projects, costs and work orders
rows.printed_heading: SCHOOL FACILITIES / John Londa, Facilities Director
rows.what_it_is: Narrative account of the year's school building projects, each with a named contractor and a cost, plus the FY14 capital request list.
rows.notes: Recoverable figures: feasibility study $750,000 approved May 2012; owner's project manager Joslin, Lesser + Associates $125,000; Passios roof designer Haynes, Leineck and Smith $9,098; roof work by M.D.M. Engineering $73,000; THMS gym snow guards $18,010; 437 work orders completed in seven months. FY14 requests: $13,800 per building x3 for HVAC controllers, $15,000 asbestos remediation, $16,000 Primary School flooring. This page also records the consolidation: Primary PreK-3, THMS 4-7, LHS 8-12, with Thomas C. Passios let to the FLLAC Collaborative's Caldwell School for roughly a third of its space — a school building moving from town use to rental income.

rows.name: Monty Tech One-Year-Out Survey: placement of the class of 2011
rows.printed_heading: One year after leaving Monty Tech, the graduates of 2011 reported the following:
rows.what_it_is: Where last year's graduates were a year after leaving, as percentages against the Carl D. Perkins Act definition of a positive placement.
rows.notes: 33% employed in a field related to their trade, 12% employed unrelated, 45% in higher education, 8% military. Sums to 98%.

rows.name: Monty Tech member towns
rows.what_it_is: The eighteen member communities of the regional district.
rows.notes: Two entries are OCR-mangled ('Ashburnnam', 'naivalu' for Harvard). Continues from p42.

rows.name: Monty Tech leadership team
rows.printed_heading: Leadership
rows.what_it_is: The ten administrators of the regional school with their titles.
rows.notes: Victoria Zarozinski's title wraps onto the next line ('Director of Student Support' / 'Services') and will read as two people unless rejoined.

rows.name: Monty Tech enrollment by member town, October 1 2011
rows.printed_heading: Enrollment
rows.what_it_is: 1,435 students broken down by each of the eighteen member towns, as a parenthesised list in a sentence.
rows.layout: prose, town name followed by count in parentheses
rows.printed_total: 1,435 students in grades nine through twelve
rows.notes: Lunenburg (72), up from 63 the previous year. Also on this page: a record 823 applications, 773 for grade 9, 380 freshmen and 24 upperclassmen admitted, VIP programme serving ~675 area students.

rows.name: Monty Tech financial report and grants
rows.printed_heading: Financial Report / Grants and Contracts
rows.what_it_is: The district's Educational Plan total and its grant income, broken into state/federal and private/competitive.
rows.notes: FY2011-2012 Educational Plan $22,744,779, a 2.4% increase; state and federal grants $1,407,959; private and competitive grants $20,918 including $13,251 from the Community Foundation of North Central Massachusetts and $7,667 from the Mass Space Grant Consortium and Nypro. The two grant streams sum to $1,428,877, which ties to the printed total.

rows.name: Monty Tech MCAS results 2010-2012, by subject
rows.printed_heading: Academic Achievement / English Language Arts | 2010 | 2011 | 2012 / Students Tested / Passing / Advanced/Proficient / Needs Improvement / Failing / Biology | 2010 | 2011 | 2012
rows.what_it_is: Parallel three-year tables for ELA, Mathematics and Biology giving students tested, passing rate and the performance distribution.
rows.grain: one performance measure for one subject in one year
rows.layout: tables side by side, split across the p44/p45 page break
rows.notes: The ELA table's header and first row are at the foot of p44 and its remaining rows at the head of p45, with the Mathematics table's rows interleaved — the four rows at the top of p45 (Advanced/Proficient 80/86/87, Needs Improvement 17/12/12, Failing 3/2/1) cannot be assigned to a subject from the OCR alone. Biology is complete and clean: tested 383/362/361, passing 95/97/98, adv-prof 68/71/73, needs improvement 27/27/24, failing 5/3/2. Narrative gives 2012 passing rates: ELA 100%, Math 99%, Biology 98%.

rows.name: Monty Tech MCAS performance by student group, with progress and performance targets
rows.printed_heading: Student Group | On Target = 75 or higher Performance | Progress
rows.what_it_is: Each reported student subgroup with its performance score and whether it met its progress target — the basis for the school's Level 1 status.
rows.columns: Student Group | Performance (On Target = 75 or higher) | Progress
rows.notes: STILL BADLY MISALIGNED. All eleven group names are present (All Students, High Needs, Low Income, ELL and Former ELL, Students with Disabilities, and six race/ethnicity groups) and five scores are present (85, 75, 79, 76, 84, 91) but the scores and the 'Met Target' flags sit on different lines from their group names and cannot be paired. Do not transcribe by row position.

rows.name: Monty Tech vocational programme enrollments
rows.what_it_is: Per-programme narrative for each of the twenty vocational areas, with enrollment and placement figures embedded.
rows.notes: The FY2012 write-ups do NOT use the '(Total enrollment: N; M males, F females)' convention that makes the FY2011 and FY2013 versions machine-readable — the figures here are scattered ('eighteen listed this program', 'eight graduating seniors report positive placements', 'seventeen students in the Class of 2012') and are often spelled out in words. Not worth extracting as a table.

rows.name: Monty Tech District School Committee membership by member town
rows.what_it_is: The regional school committee with each member's town.

rows.name: Combined balance sheet, all fund types, June 30 2012
rows.printed_heading: RECEIVABLES: / TOTAL ASSETS / LIABILITIES and FUND EQUITY: / LIABILITIES: / TOTAL LIABILITIES / FUND BALANCES: / UNRESERVED: / TOTAL FUND EQUITY / TOTAL LIABILITIES/FUND EQUITY
rows.what_it_is: Assets, liabilities and fund equity at year end across six fund-type columns.
rows.layout: row label at left, six money columns
rows.notes: Materially better than FY2011's: the RECEIVABLES section heading survives and the page runs 70 lines. Still missing: the CASH section above RECEIVABLES, and the column headers naming the six funds. Every TOTAL row prints its VALUES on the line ABOVE its own label (values on line 31, 'TOTAL ASSETS' on line 32), so a naive line-by-line read attaches each total to the wrong row. TOTAL ASSETS equals TOTAL LIABILITIES/FUND EQUITY, an internal check. LONG TERM DEBT $26,479,505 ties to the p75 debt table.

rows.name: General fund revenues pie chart, FY12
rows.printed_heading: GENERAL FUND REVENUES FY 12
rows.what_it_is: Pie chart of general fund revenue by source with percentage labels.
rows.notes: STILL BADLY DAMAGED — 9 lines, three slices: ALL OTHER 7.03%, STATE-LOCAL AID 22.23%, MOTOR VEHICLE EXCISE 4.52%. The property tax slice is absent. All the underlying figures are in the p58 receipts table.

rows.name: FY 2012 receipts, line by line
rows.printed_heading: FY 2012 RECEIPTS - JUNE 2012 / TAXES & EXCISES: / INTEREST: / DEMANDS: / FEES: / DEPARTMENTAL REVENUE: / LICENSES/PERMITS: / STATE REVENUE: / FINES & FORFEITS: / EARNINGS ON INVESTMENTS:

rows.notes: Columns one and two are clean; the third column's amounts are missing exactly as in FY2011 (DOG FINES, SALE OF TOWN PROPERTY/EQUIPMENT, SCHOOL BASED MEDICARE REIMB, MEDICARE PART D, LOCK UP FEES, MISC. REVENUE, PREMIUM SALE OF BONDS, INVESTMENT INCOME, PRIOR YEAR EXCISE, PRIOR YEAR INT/DEMAND, TRANSFERS FROM OTHER FUNDS all print label only). A few second-column labels also sit one line away from their amount. Key figures: REAL ESTATE TAXES $18,071,378.17, MOTOR VEHICLE EXCISE $1,286,412.15, CH 70 SCHOOL AID $4,612,665.00 (up from $4,523,464 in FY2011), LOTTERY/BEANO $829,777.00 (DOWN from $894,449), MSBA REIMB-SCHOOL $499,098.00 (identical to FY2011), ICE STORM/FLOODING REIMBURSEMENT $142,196.00, BUILDING PERMITS $96,279.50 (down from $181,516.40). New account lines appear this year: ADDITIONAL AID, VETERANS BENEFITS REIMBURSEMENT, STUDENT PARKING FEES, MECHANICAL PERMITS, BETTERMENT QUOTE.

rows.name: Summary of receipts by category
rows.printed_heading: SUMMARY OF RECEIPTS / TAXES & EXCISES / FEES / LICENSES AND PERMITS / STATE REVENUE / SPECIAL ASSESSMENTS / FINES & FORFEITS / INVESTMENT INCOME / TRANSFER FROM OTHER FUNDS / NON RECURRING REVENUE / GRAND TOTAL

rows.layout: right-hand column of the same landscape page
rows.printed_total: GRAND TOTAL (label present, value not captured)
rows.notes: STILL DAMAGED in exactly the way FY2011's is: all ten labels, no values. The GRAND TOTAL that would reconcile the receipts detail is missing in both years.

rows.name: General fund expenditures pie chart, FY2012
rows.printed_heading: GENERAL FUND EXPENDITURES FY 2012
rows.what_it_is: Pie chart of general fund spending by function.
